summary: The note describes ten strategies communities are using to raise low voter turnout ahead of the municipal elections on November 5th, 2023. It covers digital campaigning, school partnerships, community events, free transit, festivals, influencers, faith groups, election bulletins, art projects and door-to-door outreach. Each strategy is tied to a named local person or program.
one_line: Ten local initiatives, from digital campaigns to free bus rides and canvassing, aim to boost turnout in the November 5th, 2023 municipal elections.
key_facts: The municipal elections are scheduled for November 5th, 2023, and past elections have seen dwindling voter participation.
Council member Maria Gomez, running for reelection, hosts Instagram Live Q&A sessions so voters can engage with her campaign promises.
The local board's official Facebook page started a "Voter Education Series" covering registration and polling station locations.
Superintendent John Lee launched the "Pre-18 Participation Program", which simulates voting and discusses local governance in high school classrooms.
Mayoral candidate Emily Rodriguez's "Civic Fun Fest" is scheduled for October 12th and includes food stalls, live music, and booths on candidates and ballot issues.
Councilman Raj Patel spearheads "Ride to Vote", offering free bus rides to and from polling stations on Election Day.
Community organizer Chloe Murphy's "I Voted" festival in the Jackson District offers local musicians, food trucks, and family activities after voting.
Baseball hero Reggie Thompson's "Take Your Base, Cast Your Vote" campaign has been a hit, especially among young adults.
Pastor Sarah Nguyen's "Faith in Democracy" initiative invites congregants to forums on civic responsibilities and electoral participation.
The Community Advisory Board issues weekly election bulletins curated by Board Secretary Tim Huang, summarizing candidate platforms and voting information.
Muralist Diego Ramirez's "Voices on Walls" project uses community murals to show voters' thoughts on local politics and spark conversation.
Activist Aisha Clark leads the "Every Vote Matters" door-to-door campaign in historically low-turnout neighborhoods, offering registration assistance and absentee ballot help.
